question: What historical taxon, time, gear, and landing-area evidence does NFRDI's reproductive study report for Sardinella pacifica in shared Manila Bay, and does it resolve a species-by-site or sample-level identification crosswalk?

sources.title: Reproductive Biology Pattern and Size at Maturity of the Newly Reclassified Sardinella pacifica (Hata & Motomura, 2019) in Manila Bay, Philippines
sources.citation: Dicdiquin, N. R. B., Lopez, G. D. V., Torres, F. S. B. Jr., Abad, J. L., Perez, J. E. G., Ruado, M. A., Loyola, C. M., Sucgang, R., & Pendre, J. E. G. (2026). Reproductive Biology Pattern and Size at Maturity of the Newly Reclassified Sardinella pacifica (Hata & Motomura, 2019) in Manila Bay, Philippines. The Philippine Journal of Fisheries, 2026 NSAP Special Issue, 171-182. https://doi.org/10.31398/tpjf/33.3.2025C0013.
locators: Printed pages 171-173: abstract, study area, eight landing sites, sampling design, and Figure 1
Printed pages 177-180: results, discussion, and conclusions on spawning, maturity size, and study recommendations
sources.accessStatus: The complete 12-page official NFRDI-hosted PDF was retrieved as application/pdf (2,550,742 bytes) and reviewed as text. Figure 1 showing selected landing centers was visually inspected. The relative link on the journal page resolved to an HTML fallback; the official /tpjf/etc/ PDF path returned the article. Local research copy is ignored by Git and is not redistributed.
sources.sourceReportedFinding: The study reports 4,073 fish samples purchased and randomly selected from eight Manila Bay fish landing sites: two in Metro Manila, two in Bataan, and four in Cavite. Landed-catch samples cover January 2017 through December 2021 and four gear types: gillnets, stationary liftnets, ring nets, and otter trawls. The authors analyze the samples under the revised name Sardinella pacifica and report year-round spawning with varying peaks, female Lm50 estimates of 10.6-11.0 cm and male estimates of 8.8-10.1 cm. The paper also recommends an 11.8 cm minimum total length as a management measure; this is the authors' study recommendation, not a verified Philippine regulation.
sources.license: CC BY-NC 4.0, stated in the article's open-access notice; attribution and noncommercial terms apply.
sources.reuseStatus: Only attributed bibliographic and concise methodological/findings metadata are retained in this research record. No article table, figure, image, or extended text is reproduced. The source's noncommercial license does not itself approve public app reuse or commercial use.

assessment.historicalLocality: Shared Manila Bay fishery and landing-site study; four of eight reported landing sites are in Cavite, with the remaining sites in Metro Manila and Bataan.
assessment.timeWindow: January 2017 through December 2021, as reported for the landed-catch data; this is a historical sampling window, not a current inventory.
assessment.evidenceType: Fishery-dependent reproductive-biology study using purchased, randomly selected fish at landing sites, attributed by the authors to fishers operating in Manila Bay.
assessment.taxonomicFinding: The study applies the name Sardinella pacifica following Hata and Motomura (2019), noting the former S. fimbriata identification. The reviewed methods do not provide voucher accessions or an individual-level specimen determination crosswalk that independently confirms every sample's reidentification.
assessment.landingAndCaptureLimits: The paper reports the number and administrative distribution of landing sites and shows selected landing centers in Figure 1. It does not report per-site sample counts, taxon-by-site counts, a gear-by-site crosswalk, or individual capture coordinates. Landing location is not the fish's exact capture location; retain only the shared Manila Bay fishery context and do not assign the taxon to a Cavite municipality, municipal water, or exact capture point.
assessment.biologicalAndManagementLimits: The reported year-round spawning pattern includes variation in peak periods; the results state that no catch was available from March through May 2020. The 11.8 cm minimum-length statement is an author recommendation in a historical study, not a current legal size limit or fishing rule. Do not turn reproductive findings into current season, bait, catchability, safety, or legal advice.
assessment.relationshipToEarlierSources: This 2017-2021 reproductive study is distinct from the 2014 pooled NFRDI ring-net length-frequency analysis. No sample or voucher linkage between those datasets is reported. The 2026 study does not independently crosswalk or relabel the older pooled Sardinella fimbriata records.
assessment.sharedWaterbodyBoundary: Manila Bay is shared among CALABARZON, NCR, and Central Luzon. The four Cavite landing sites are not four proven Cavite capture locations for the analyzed S. pacifica specimens. No official bay or municipal-water boundary is asserted.

decision.reason: The source directly studies S. pacifica landed from Manila Bay fishers across 2017-2021 and identifies four Cavite landing sites, but supplies no per-site taxon counts, capture-ground crosswalk, or voucher-level reidentification trail. The evidence is valuable historical shared-bay fishery context, not current presence or municipality-level occurrence.

limitations: The source reports landing sites, not individual capture coordinates or a complete species-by-site crosswalk.
No sample counts per landing center, site-specific gear counts, or site-by-year taxon matrix were reported in the reviewed text.
No specimen voucher accessions or sample-level taxonomic re-examination crosswalk were reported in the reviewed methods.
This historical fishery-dependent study does not establish current presence, abundance, diet, catchability, water safety, legal fishing status, or a complete Manila Bay species inventory.
The 11.8 cm minimum-size statement is a study recommendation, not verified regulation; current law requires separate authoritative verification.
The article is CC BY-NC 4.0; source attribution and license limits apply, and no public app content is approved by this research review.
nextAction: If a source-backed municipal or gear-specific record is needed, request the underlying NSAP sample/site/gear/year matrix, species identification protocol, voucher or reference-specimen accessions, and applicable data reuse terms through an official NFRDI route. Keep this source linked to shared Manila Bay only while those crosswalks remain unavailable.
